newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine credit cards growing 30-40 pct annually.
newsitem.headline: Philippine credit cards growing 30-40 pct annually.

text.p: The credit card business in the Philippines is booming with growth rates seen at 30 to 40 percent annually, a Citibank official said on Monday.

The growth comes on top of a threefold increase in the size of the business in the past three years, Harpal Dugal, vice president and business manager for Citibank's credit card divison in the Philippines told Reuters in an interview.
Total spending through credit cards had now gone up to 45 billion to 50 billion pesos annually from 16 billion to 18 billion pesos in 1993, he said.
"(Rate of) growth is slowing down because the base is much higher, but it is definitely outdoing growth in most industries," Dugal said.
Citibank Philippines, a unit of Citicorp, dominates the business with its cards accounting for 14 billion to 15 billion pesos out of the total spending of 45 billion to 50 billion.
Dugal said Citibank's card base in the Philippines was about 400,000 compared to about 360,000 cards issued by its nearest rival Equitable, a local group comprising 16 banks.
The credit-revolving rate, which is the best indicator of profit margins, was among the highest in the Philippines, Dugal said.
"Citibank's outstandings have crossed 6.5 billion pesos as of August. I think some of our closest competitors are in the 2.0 billion to 2.5 billion region. So we are way bigger," Dugal said.

Dugal declined to give profit figures for Citibank's credit cards business in the Philippines but said it accounted for about 65 to 70 percent of the profits of its consumer banking division and about 30 to 35 percent of total profits from the Philippines.
"Citibank's balance sheet shows credit cards is the number one business worldwide," he said.
Of 1995 profits of over $3.0 billion, 30 to 35 percent would have come from credit cards, he said.
